findings.title: Read the transcription model from a typed request
findings.description: This new request-body access violates R-11 in PROJECT_RULES.md: "Request bodies and query parameters in the sidecar server must be declared as typed models or typed parameters; handlers must not read raw untyped dictionaries from a request." The model selection input is currently read from the raw dict parameter. `git diff --unified=50 HEAD~1 HEAD -- src-tauri/sidecar/server.py` confirms this line was added.

findings.title: Model deletion endpoint has no behavioral integration coverage
findings.description: The new endpoint removes cached revisions, clears category-specific in-memory model references, invalidates the status cache, and has distinct unknown, not-downloaded, and failure responses. The added integration tests only inspect registry constants, while the frontend test only checks that the Tauri command is invoked; none exercises this endpoint against a controlled Hugging Face cache. Regressions could leave a model reported as installed or loaded after deletion, or break deletion/error responses without a test failing.

findings.title: Annotate the model deletion handler return type
findings.description: The new Python handler has a parameter annotation but no return annotation, contrary to R-12 in PROJECT_RULES.md: "Python functions must carry type hints on parameters and return values". `git diff --unified=50 HEAD~1 HEAD -- src-tauri/sidecar/server.py` confirms this is a new function.

findings.title: Model deletion blocks the async server loop
findings.description: `delete_model` is an async FastAPI handler, but it executes Hugging Face cache deletion synchronously on the event-loop thread. Removing a large speech model can take long enough to stall other sidecar requests, including generation polling and health/status checks. Run the deletion in a worker thread, as the download path does for its blocking work.

findings.title: Deleting a model can invalidate an active generation
findings.description: The generation worker awaits thread-backed Qwen calls between segments, and voice conversion also awaits thread-backed chunk conversions. A concurrent delete request clears these module globals while a job is in progress; subsequent Qwen segments can fail the `Qwen model not loaded` check, and an in-flight voice-conversion thread can dereference the cleared model. Defer unloading until the model is idle or synchronize deletion with active jobs.

findings.title: Add type hints to the new Python test methods
findings.description: The added test methods in this file omit parameter and return annotations, contrary to R-12 in PROJECT_RULES.md: "Python functions must carry type hints on parameters and return values". The same unannotated pattern is used by the other new test methods in this hunk. `git diff --unified=50 HEAD~1 HEAD -- src-tauri/sidecar/test_server_integration.py` confirms the method is new.

findings.title: Transcription model test checks bookkeeping instead of the loaded model
findings.description: This test passes when the requested name is merely copied into `_whisper_model_name`; it never asserts that `load_model` received the mapped `mlx-community/whisper-medium-mlx` repo or that transcription ran through the loaded model. The new selectable-model behavior can therefore regress to loading the default or a wrong repo while this test still passes. Assert the loader argument and cover request propagation through the sidecar endpoint so the user-selected model is actually used.

findings.title: Whisper model IDs are duplicated across the server and engine
findings.description: The sidecar's model registry in server.py also maps these same transcription names to Hugging Face repo IDs. Download/status handling reads that registry, while transcription resolves the configured name through this separate map. If either entry changes independently, the UI can report or download one repository while the pipeline tries to load another. Move the canonical model definitions to a small shared sidecar module imported by both server.py and tts.py, keeping HTTP routing out of the engine dependency path.

findings.title: Reject transcription model names outside the registry (OWASP A08)
findings.description: The new /transcribe and /transcribe-path request fields flow into this function, and unknown names fall through as Hugging Face repository IDs that are passed to load_stt_model. A caller able to reach the unauthenticated loopback sidecar can therefore make it fetch and load an arbitrary repository; this also replaces the process-wide cached Whisper model used by later pipeline transcriptions. Reject model names absent from WHISPER_MODELS and only pass the corresponding registry repo_id to the loader.

findings.title: Add a behavior test for the model deletion command
findings.description: R-16 in PROJECT_RULES.md requires: "Every new public function, command, or component with logic must have a test in the same change". The new Tauri command handles the deletion request and response parsing, but the only added `delete_model` coverage in `src/lib/voicebox.test.ts` asserts that the frontend wrapper invokes the command; no test exercises this command's behavior. `rg -n 'delete_model|deleteModel' src-tauri/sidecar/test_server_integration.py src-tauri/src/models.rs src/lib/voicebox.test.ts` confirms there is no endpoint or Rust command test.

findings.title: Avoid an explicit any cast in the model status test
findings.description: The explicit `any` cast violates R-01 in PROJECT_RULES.md: "TypeScript code must compile under `strict` mode without `any`, `@ts-ignore`, or non-null assertions (`!`) unless a comment on the same line gives the reason." This test already receives the typed `VoiceboxModelStatus[]` result, so the cast is unnecessary; no same-line exception comment is present. `git diff --unified=50 HEAD~1 HEAD -- src/lib/voicebox.test.ts` confirms this line is new.

findings.title: Duplicate Code: Required model policy is repeated across screens
findings.description: The same mode-to-required-model rule is independently implemented in this prerequisite check, `downloadModels`, the wizard's status display, and the settings button. If the required set changes, updating only some copies can make the wizard claim setup is complete while another screen still requests different models. Put the mode-to-model selection in one shared helper and use its result for these checks and displays.

findings.title: Document the new model management behavior
findings.description: The change adds a user-facing Models page for downloading, selecting, and deleting local models, but no README or documentation file is included in `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD`. This violates R-20 in PROJECT_RULES.md: "User-visible behavior changes must update the README or docs in the same change." The changed page heading anchors the new behavior; the command output confirms no documentation was updated.

findings.title: Required model policy is repeated across the settings and wizard pages
findings.description: The settings page repeats the same transcription-plus-local-mode model selection implemented in create-voice/+page.svelte (and repeated again there for prerequisite checks, downloads, and display). These views can drift when model requirements change: Settings may allow voice creation while the wizard blocks it, or vice versa. Put the required-model selection in one shared frontend helper and have both pages use it.

findings.title: Report model status check failures
findings.description: The catch deliberately suppresses the model status error. R-05 in PROJECT_RULES.md requires every awaited IPC or network failure to be reported to the user or rethrown, and forbids empty catches. Here a failed check silently leaves the model list empty and makes the settings button show Setup Models. `git diff --unified=60 HEAD~1 HEAD -- 'src/routes/(app)/settings/+page.svelte'` confirms this catch was added.
